mainEntity.name: How much does a Land Rover Defender 110 TD5 engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A fully rebuilt Land Rover Defender 110 TD5 engine typically costs between £3,500 and £5,500 for supply only, with supply and fit packages ranging from £4,500 to £6,500 depending on the specialist.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of head gasket failure in a Land Rover Defender 110 TD5?

acceptedAnswer.text: The early TD5 10P is prone to head gasket issues due to plastic locating dowels. Early warning signs include white smoke from the exhaust, unexplained coolant loss, oil that looks like mayonnaise under the filler cap, or overheating under load.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the TD5 10P and TD5 15P engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: The primary difference lies in reliability upgrades introduced during production. The TD5 10P used plastic head locating dowels, which were prone to shearing, while the TD5 15P introduced steel locating dowels and a revised injector loom design.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a classic Land Rover Defender 110 TD5?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, investing in a rebuilt engine is financially sound for most owners. With classic Land Rover Defender 110 values currently ranging from £8,000 to over £25,000 depending on specification, a replacement preserves the vehicle's value and provides a reliable, warrantied powertrain.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Land Rover Defender 110 TD5 engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A standard supply and fit service for a Land Rover Defender 110 TD5 typically takes 2 to 3 days at a specialist workshop. This includes removing the old unit, preparing the replacement, installation, and initial running-in checks.

historyTimeline.h2: Land Rover Defender 110 TD5 - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: When the TD5 launched in the Defender 110, it replaced the naturally aspirated 300Tdi, bringing electronic fuel injection and improved refinement while retaining the legendary off-road durability of the classic chassis.

milestones.description: TD5 10P, 2.5L, 122hp (Initial launch with electronic injection; later known for plastic dowel head gasket vulnerabilities)
TD5 15P, 2.5L, 122hp (Major revision introducing steel head locating dowels and a revised injector loom to prevent ECU oil contamination)
End of TD5 production for the classic Defender 110, replaced by the Ford-sourced 2.4 TDCi (244DT) Puma engine.

commonProblems.h2: Land Rover Defender 110 TD5 Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Land Rover Defender 110 TD5 is celebrated for its torque and mechanical simplicity, but two well-documented design flaws require attention. The TD5 10P and 15P engines dominate replacement demand for this era, primarily due to head gasket and injector loom failures. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing these original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Head Gasket Failure - Why the Land Rover Defender 110 TD5 (10P) Head Gasket Fails Prematurely
problems.rootCause: The early TD5 10P used plastic locating dowels between the block and cylinder head. Under thermal stress, these can shear, allowing the head to shift and blow the head gasket.

repairOptions.tier: Head Gasket Replacement (with steel dowel upgrade)
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Stripping the top end, machining the head, fitting steel dowels and a new gasket.
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if the block and head are not warped or cracked.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of a fully rebuilt TD5 with steel dowels as standard, plus 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended for high-mileage units or if overheating has caused secondary damage.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical Land Rover Defender 110 TD5 (1998-2006) currently holds a value of £8,000-£25,000+ in the UK, depending on specification and condition [THIRD-PARTY]. This places most examples in the £8,000-£15,000 or £15,000+ bands, meaning a £3,500-£5,500 rebuilt engine replacement is typically a small fraction of the vehicle's worth and is highly recommended to preserve the asset. Flag: Safe.
problems.recommendation: If the engine has high mileage or shows signs of overheating, a full rebuild with a steel-dowel modified head gasket setup is the most reliable long-term solution. A simple gasket swap on an aged 10P block risks repeat failure.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt TD5 10P Land Rover Defender 110 TD5 engine prices

problems.h4: Injector Loom Oil Leak - Why the Land Rover Defender 110 TD5 ECU Gets Contaminated
problems.rootCause: The injector wiring harness gasket degrades over time, allowing oil from the rocker cover to wick along the wires and pool inside the Engine Control Unit (ECU), causing electrical faults or complete ECU failure.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacing the harness and rocker cover gasket, plus cleaning the ECU.
repairOptions.longevity: Highly effective preventative fix if caught early before ECU damage occurs.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of a fully rebuilt TD5 with a new, upgraded injector loom fitted as standard, plus 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: Best if the ECU has already been damaged or the engine has high mileage alongside the leak.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: As noted, classic Defender 110 values (£8,000-£25,000+) easily absorb the cost of a full rebuild, making it a sound investment over repeated electrical repairs.
problems.recommendation: For an isolated loom leak with a healthy ECU, a specialist harness and gasket replacement is highly cost-effective. However, if the ECU is already damaged or the engine has high mileage, a rebuilt unit provides a comprehensive, warrantied reset.
